idiom_name: template/per-aggregate class returning std::vector / std::optional, delegating to a hand-written mapper
implementation_notes: The standard library supplies the collection vocabulary but no persistence, so the repository is a hand-written class (often a template on the aggregate) whose methods return std::vector<Invoice> / std::optional<Invoice> and delegate to a mapper object that owns the SQL and the row-to-object conversion. Use std::optional for find-by-id so the interface has no nullable-pointer trap, and take the mapper as a template or policy parameter when only the storage backend varies at compile time. Frameworks such as SOCI or ODB provide the mapper half, but the domain-facing interface, its lifetime rules and the test double are still written by hand.
pitfalls: Returning a reference into a container that dies at the end of the call (const std::vector<Invoice>& to a temporary, or std::string_view over a mapper buffer) is the classic lifetime bug; return by value or hand out owned storage.
Polymorphic repositories need virtual ~InvoiceRepository() = default, otherwise deleting through the base interface is undefined behaviour.
Templating the whole repository per aggregate multiplies instantiations and compile time; when only the mapper varies, parameterise the mapper instead of the repository.
